facts.fact: WHO's SCORE assessment rates Zambia 'Complete' on a standardised system of electronic data entry for aggregate reporting at the district or comparable level, on data from 2013 to 2018; it does not say whether any facility enters its own reports.

WHO's SCORE assessment puts completeness of reporting by public primary care facilities, and by public hospitals, above 75%, and by private facilities at 25% to 75%, on data from 2013 to 2018; it gives no count or share of facilities entering their own reports.

WHO's SCORE assessment rates as 'Not there' a system of electronic capture of patient-level health data in primary care facilities that is standardised and fully interoperable with the aggregate routine system, on data from 2013 to 2018; the rating is of a standardised interoperable system, not of every electronic record.
facts.system: Electronic capture of patient-level health data

facts.fact: WHO's SCORE assessment rates as 'Partial' a system of electronic capture of patient-level health data in hospitals that is standardised and fully interoperable with the aggregate routine system, on data from 2013 to 2018; it does not say which hospitals or how many.
facts.system: Electronic capture of patient-level health data

systems.tiers: electronic aggregate entry at district or comparable level; public primary care facilities and public hospitals reporting above 75% complete

systems.system: Electronic capture of patient-level health data
systems.tiers: hospitals: partial; primary care facilities: not there

systems.system: National human resources for health information system

note: A checklist of ratings with no system named; the system labels are the assessment's own criteria. It also records a national eHealth strategy as existing, without naming any system it covers.
